entries.definition: what someone thinks about a subject
entries.example: My opinion changed after I listened to the other group.

entries.definition: a thought or suggested possibility
entries.example: Her idea was to share tools instead of buying more.

entries.definition: reasons offered to support a point of view
entries.example: His argument includes examples from the class survey.

entries.definition: an explanation for an action or belief
entries.example: The main reason for the change was safety.

entries.definition: something that can be established as true
entries.example: We checked each fact before publishing the guide.

entries.definition: something a person accepts as true
entries.example: Her belief about the route came from an old map.

entries.definition: a statement that something is true and may need proof
entries.example: The report gives no evidence for its central claim.

entries.definition: a feeling of uncertainty about something
entries.example: The missing date raised doubt about the photograph’s meaning.

entries.definition: feeling confident that something is true
entries.example: Are you sure this is the most recent timetable?

entries.definition: known or believed without serious doubt
entries.example: We are certain that the room was locked at noon.

entries.definition: able to happen or be done
entries.example: A shorter route is possible if the bridge is open.

entries.definition: unable to happen or be done
entries.example: It is impossible to finish safely without the correct tools.

entries.definition: expected to happen or be true
entries.example: A clear sign is likely to reduce confusion.

entries.definition: not expected to happen or be true
entries.example: Rain is unlikely this afternoon, but we packed a cover.

entries.definition: to choose after thinking about possibilities
entries.example: We must decide which problem to investigate first.

entries.definition: the act of selecting between possibilities
entries.example: The choice depends on the time and money available.

entries.definition: one of the possibilities available
entries.example: Taking an evening class is another option.

entries.definition: a feature that makes one choice more useful
entries.example: The main advantage of the smaller bag is its weight.

entries.definition: a feature that makes a situation or choice less useful
entries.example: The long journey is one disadvantage of the new location.

entries.definition: a useful or helpful result
entries.example: Sharing the tools brought a benefit to every group.

entries.definition: a problem that reduces the value of something
entries.example: The only drawback is that the room closes early.

entries.definition: a situation that needs an answer or improvement
entries.example: We described the problem before suggesting any equipment.

entries.definition: a way to deal with a problem
entries.example: The simplest solution was to move the sign.

entries.definition: a task or situation that is difficult but worth attempting
entries.example: Explaining the idea without pictures was a useful challenge.

entries.definition: requiring effort or skill
entries.example: The difficult question made us look at our evidence again.

entries.definition: easy to understand or not complicated
entries.example: A simple diagram can explain the order of events.

entries.definition: having several connected parts that need careful understanding
entries.example: The team divided the complex task into smaller steps.

entries.definition: an arrangement of actions intended to achieve an aim
entries.example: Our plan includes a test before the final decision.

entries.definition: to use your mind to consider something
entries.example: Think about who will use the sign before designing it.

entries.definition: to think about something before making a decision
entries.example: We should consider how the change affects evening workers.

entries.definition: to form a picture or possibility in your mind
entries.example: Imagine using this route while carrying a heavy bag.

entries.definition: to think something may be true without being sure
entries.example: I suppose the office may close earlier today.

entries.definition: to think about something because you want to know more
entries.example: I wonder why the two measurements are different.

entries.definition: to become aware of something
entries.example: I did not realize the map showed last year’s route.

entries.definition: to think that something will probably happen
entries.example: We expect more visitors when the weather improves.

entries.definition: to give an answer without enough information to be sure
entries.example: Do not guess the dose from the color of the bottle.

entries.definition: to examine something to find out if it is correct
entries.example: Please check the date before sharing the announcement.

entries.definition: to give particular attention to something
entries.example: Let us focus on the problem we can solve today.

entries.definition: careful thought or notice given to something
entries.example: The unusual result deserves closer attention.

entries.definition: the ability to remember information or past experiences
entries.example: A written note can support your memory.

entries.definition: to bring information or an experience back to mind
entries.example: I remember the route better when I draw it.

entries.definition: to fail to remember something
entries.example: I sometimes forget a name but recognize the face.

entries.definition: to gain knowledge or ability through experience or study
entries.example: We can learn from a test that does not work.

entries.definition: to find something previously unknown to you
entries.example: We may discover another explanation by asking more questions.

entries.definition: to make something new
entries.example: The group will create a map of safe walking routes.

entries.definition: to make or design something that did not exist before
entries.example: The students tried to invent a simple bottle holder.

entries.definition: to show or make a link between things
entries.example: The diagram helps connect the cause with its effect.

entries.definition: to keep things apart or distinguish between them
entries.example: We separate observations from guesses in our notes.

entries.definition: to arrange things or activities in a useful order
entries.example: Please organize the questions by topic before the meeting.

entries.definition: something a person or group aims to achieve
entries.example: Our goal is to make the instructions easier to follow.
